hypothesis: In the FC 0x17 (write-and-read registers) handler, the address validation tests `mapping_address < 0` twice and never tests `mapping_address_write < 0`. A client can send a write address below `start_registers` (for example a non-zero start_registers with write address 0). The validation passes, and the write loop then stores attacker-controlled 16-bit values at negative indices of `tab_registers`. This is a heap out-of-bounds write (the CVE-2022-0367 pattern).
evidence_source: Lines 962-965: `mapping_address < 0 || (mapping_address + nb) > nb_registers || mapping_address < 0 || (mapping_address_write + nb_write) > nb_registers`. Line 953 computes `mapping_address_write = address_write - start_registers`, which can be negative. Lines 978-982 loop `for (i = mapping_address_write; ...) mb_mapping->tab_registers[i] = ...`.

expected_behavior: Heap-buffer-overflow (underflow) write before the start of tab_registers, reported by ASan. It corrupts adjacent heap memory and may crash the server.
